item.title: Under the Microscope Podcast: Amplifying the Technology Scientists Use to Accelerate Discovery
item.description:
Client: Park Systems
Service Provider: Dr. Pranoti Kshirsagar (The Science Talk)
Service: Science Podcast as a Service
Execution Period: 5 May 2025 to 19 May 2025

Executive Summary

The Under the Microscope podcast showcases innovative approaches to align research stakeholders, acting as an amplifier for the innovative technology scientists use to accelerate research and discovery. In this episode, Park Systems’ NX10 Atomic Force Microscope (AFM) appeared where it matters most: inside real research by Martin Rejhon at Charles University in Prague. One episode became 11 content assets across channels, generating more than 10,000 social media views and a 6% engagement rate on LinkedIn within two weeks.

item.title: How to add AI disclosures that comply with the EU AI Act
item.description: The EU AI Act’s transparency obligations under Article 50 apply from 2 August 2026. If you publish AI-generated content professionally, you have specific disclosure duties. These duties go well beyond a footnote in your terms and conditions. The European Commission published draft guidelines that explain what disclosures must look like, where they must appear, and what does not meet the standard. This guide translates those requirements into practical placement guidance for content creators, freelancers, and science communicators.

item.title: Stop Chasing Platforms. Own Your Audience Instead.
item.description: I know what it feels like to build something real on a platform, and then watch it disappear. For years, I ran RealScientists Nano, a rotation curation account. Each week, a new materials or nanoscientist took over the account. Each host shared their research, their life in the lab, and their questions. More than 120 scientists from around the world took part. During the pandemic, the account became a genuine lifeline. It gave scientists a space to connect, to laugh, and to feel less isolated.
